name: Steve Jobs Product Lens
philosophy: The customer's experience is the product. Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication. A thousand good ideas must be killed so the essential few can live. Design is not how it looks; it is how it works. People do not know what they want until you show it to them, but you must understand them deeply enough to know what to show.
evidence: iPod/iPhone removed features competitors advertised (FM radio, removable battery) to make the core experience obvious.
Original iPhone launched without copy/paste because the team had not found the right design yet; refusing to ship a bad version is a feature.
strengths: Questioning complexity added for internal convenience
blind_spots: May undervalue power-user or enterprise feature needs
Can be impatient with gradual rollout and learning loops
May ignore regulatory, security, or CFO constraints unless explicitly added
performs_well: Feature prioritization when resources are constrained
performs_poorly: Deep workflow customization for expert users

disagreement_profile.typical_conflict: Removing features can reduce short-term addressable market.
Competitors may use missing features as sales ammunition.
